attributes.law_screen: claim.law.point-of-use-single-use-pointer-delay.20260830.v1 APPLIED as AXIS1 - this function matches the law's stated precondition shape almost exactly (a local pointer computed from an ADDR16-relocated global, initialized at function entry, read only later in the body), and it is the law that identified the residual in the first place. attributes.residual: SCHEDULE/REGISTER_ONLY, real 198, 254/254 instructions, opcode multiset IDENTICAL. Two coupled facts, both precisely located. (1) ADDR16_LO PLACEMENT: target emits `lis r6,0 @lbl_801174A8(HA)` at +0x4, then defers `addi r30,r6,0 @lbl_801174A8(LO)` to +0x18, i.e. AFTER the `stwu`/`stmw` frame setup and directly into the final callee-saved home r30. Ours emits `addi r6,r6,0 @LO` at +0xc, before `stwu`, folding LO into the same scratch register, and then materializes the callee-saved copy separately at +0x18 as `addi r29,r6,0`. Instruction COUNT is unaffected (254/254, multiset identical) because the target spends its balancing addi later at +0x374 (`addi r29,r4,0`); fndiff's aligner pairs our +0xc addi against that +0x374 addi, which is why the --ops summary reads as one insert plus one delete rather than as a move. (2) ROLE SWAP: target assigns strs=r30 and hres=r29, ours strs=r29 and hres=r30, and that two-register transposition propagates through the body (e.g. target `lwz r6,40(r26)` / `mr r24,r0` where ours has `lwz r8,40(r26)` / `mr r25,r0`). AXES TRIED: AXIS1 point-of-use deferral of `strs = lbl_801174A8;` to immediately before the fileRemaining if/else - REGRESSED, multiset broke to DIFFERS (+2 addi / -2 mr), reverted. AXIS2 swap the `hres`/`strs` declaration order - byte-NEUTRAL, real stayed exactly 198, reverted. Not yet tried and the natural next axes for a follow-up session: forcing the HA/LO split by giving the pool base a second independent consumer, and re-testing AXIS1 at intermediate deferral distances (one statement at a time rather than past the whole ring-cursor block), since the overshoot shows the effect is distance-sensitive rather than binary. This function is NOT yet exhausted - two axes only, and the residual still has a source-shaped component (the LO placement), so it is not yet a clean WEBFRANK candidate the way LineLineDist is.
